articles.title: Edward Gastfriend, Holocaust Survivor Who Helped Create Early Memorial, Dies at 100
articles.mainIdea: Edward Gastfriend, Holocaust Survivor Who Helped Create Early Memorial, Dies at 100
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal: Edward Gastfriend, Holocaust Survivor Who Helped Create Early Memorial, Dies at 100. As a Jewish teenager in Poland, he was able to pose as a gentile, eluding capture while working with other young people resisting Nazi rule in the early stages of World War II. After he was caught and sent to a series of prison camps, his quick wits allowed him to spot opportunities to secure scraps of food and find the least-dangerous forms of forced labor. Gastfriend, who died Nov. 18 in Delray Beach, Fla., at the age of 100, emigrated to Philadelphia in 1947 and made a living by running retail-clothing stores and investing in rental properties. Gastfriend was vice chairman of a committee that raised money and won civic approval for one of the earliest Holocaust memorials in the U.S.—the Monument to Six Million Jewish Martyrs, a bronze sculpture by Nathan Rapoport, installed in central Philadelphia in 1964.
